channel.name: Fix-It Forest
channel.tagline: Little repairs, one at a time.
channel.description:
In a hollow stump at the edge of the birch wood, Mango the fox runs a very small repair shop.

Every episode, a friend brings her one broken thing — a wobbly stool, a kite that will not fly, a music box that plays too slowly. Mango works out what went wrong, fixes it, and names the idea that made it work, in words a small child can repeat.

Gentle, unhurried stories about noticing, mending, and putting things right. Made for preschoolers and the grown-ups watching with them.

New repair every day.
channel.naming_notes: Channel is named for the format and setting, not the character, so the cast can widen without a rename. 'Mango' was deliberately kept out of the channel name — the Mango Kids namespace already has several established channels and competing there for search would repeat the nursery-rhyme mistake.

series.title: Fix-It Forest
series.logline: A team of five forest fixers, each good at a different kind of problem, mends one broken thing together every episode.
series.why_this_survives_policy: One authored property with a fixed cast, a fixed visual style and a fixed 5-beat structure. Every episode is a genuinely different repair with a different physical principle, produced against a dedupe gate. That is the opposite of near-duplicate mass production — the standard YouTube's inauthentic-content policy actually enforces.
series.runtime_rationale: Long-form (3-5 min) is where kids watch time and revenue actually live; Shorts are cut from each episode for discovery. See docs/youtube-kids-shorts-niche-research.md §2.1.
series.made_for_kids_rationale: Content is child-directed — a talking animal fixing toys for a preschool audience. COPPA requires the label; mislabelling risks ~$53k/violation. Accept the ~$1-3 RPM and treat Shorts as the discovery engine per the research doc §2.1.
series.format_note: Ensemble-of-specialists structure, a long-standing genre convention. Original cast, world and designs throughout — no borrowed characters, names, uniforms, vehicles or visual language from any existing property.

mango.role: lead — works out WHY it broke
mango.look: rust-orange fur, cream chest, one ear permanently folded at the tip, green canvas apron with four pockets
mango.voice_direction: warm, unhurried, mid-register, a smile in the tone
mango.catch_behaviour: turns the broken thing over twice before saying anything

bramble.look: dusty brown, round glasses too big for his face, a red neckerchief
bramble.catch_behaviour: worries out loud so someone can reassure him

tolly.look: broad, charcoal and cream striped face, rolled shirtsleeves, a wooden mallet through the belt
tolly.catch_behaviour: tests everything by leaning on it

wren.role: height and air — anything up high, anything that flies
wren.look: tiny, warm brown with a cream eye-stripe, a twine tool-belt
wren.catch_behaviour: always arrives last and from above

pip.role: small spaces — reaches what nobody else can
pip.look: pale gold, enormous ears, wears a thimble as a helmet
pip.catch_behaviour: narrates what she finds inside things

world.setting: a hollow stump workshop at the edge of a birch wood, lit by one round window
props_that_recur: the notice board where jobs arrive
world.time_of_day: always warm late afternoon — keeps lighting consistent across episodes

visual_style.medium: 2D storybook gouache, visible paper grain, soft edges
visual_style.line: no hard outlines; forms defined by colour blocks and shadow
visual_style.camera: locked-off mid shots and one close-up on the hands at the fix moment
visual_style.text_on_screen: one short caption per beat, bottom third, never covering hands
visual_style.consistency_rule: Every generation prompt must include the cast look block verbatim plus the palette. Character drift across episodes is the single most visible sign of machine production.

episode_formula.engine: Someone brings a broken thing. Mango works out the real cause. The cause names a DOMAIN, and the domain names which teammate is needed. A first attempt fails for an honest reason. The right teammate solves it. The principle is named in plain words.
episode_formula.why_it_scales: Five domains x objects x causes x who-brings-it is a very large space, and the failed first attempt adds a second independent axis. The team is generative, not decorative: the physics picks the character, so no episode can be a reskin of another.

beats.name: cold-open
beats.content: The thing breaks, on screen, in use. No dialogue needed.

beats.name: the-call
beats.content: It arrives at the den. Whoever is there reacts. Establish stakes: who needs it, and when.

beats.name: diagnose
beats.content: Mango turns it over twice and names the actual cause. Close on the fault.

beats.name: first-try
beats.content: An obvious fix is tried and honestly fails. No blame, no one is foolish.

beats.name: who-is-needed
beats.content: The cause names a domain; the domain names a teammate. They arrive in character.

beats.name: the-fix
beats.content: The real repair, as process. Two characters working together. This is the retention beat.

beats.name: the-test
beats.content: Tested in the same use that broke it in beat 1. It works.

beats.name: name-it
beats.content: The principle stated once, plainly, in words a four-year-old can repeat.

episode_formula.shot_constraint: Veo renders only 4, 6 or 8 second clips. Beat durations must therefore be even and at least 4s, so the shot planner can compose each beat exactly.

hard_rules: Never a villain, never a character who broke the object on purpose, never blame.
The fix must be physically real. A child watching must not learn something false.
Never depict a repair a child could copy dangerously — no blades, heat, electricity, small swallowable magnets, or climbing.
The first attempt fails for an honest physical reason, never because a character was careless or silly.
One principle per episode, named in plain words, never jargon.
No brand names, no real-world product lookalikes, no resemblance to any existing kids property.
Nobody is ever the butt of a joke. Pip is the youngest, never the punchline.
No character asks the audience to like, subscribe or follow.

dedupe_axes.comment: Enforced by pipeline/lib/registry.mjs, not by trusting the model.

domain.note: rotate which teammate leads the fix

owner.note: rotate who brings the job in

cause.note: the reason it broke must vary

failed_attempt.note: the first try that fails must vary

dedupe_axes.similarity_note: Combined trigram+token similarity against every prior premise.
